summary: Corporate proxy injects Authorization header, causing S3 presigned model downloads to 403 in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 403 failures when Redwood Private edge attempts to fetch model artifacts from S3 using presigned URLs. Failures started after the customer's corporate proxy was deployed for egress inspection last week. Downloads intermittently succeed, but a large percentage of model pulls return 403 Forbidden from the S3 origin.

Impact:
- Model pulls for new worker nodes fail ~40% of the time, causing pod bootstrapping to take significantly longer and causing inference capacity to lag during scaling events.
- Affected customer is on Private deployment (VPC peered with Redwood control plane). Production traffic intermittently retries and falls back to older model cache, increasing latency and token cost.

Environment:
- Customer: Acme Analytics (private)
- Region: us-east-1 (peered VPC)
- Redwood private deploy version: 2026.02.11
- Proxy: corporate inline HTTP(S) proxy (squid-based) performing header injection and request logging; vendor-managed.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a new worker boot in customer VPC (simulated by deleting a serving pod).
2) Observe the control-plane presigned-url issued to the runner in logs (URL is to s3.amazonaws.com with X-Amz-Signature params).
3) Runner attempts GET to presigned URL via customer egress path (through corporate proxy).
4) Proxy rewrites the request, adding an Authorization: Basic <redacted> header and forwards to S3.
5) S3 returns 403 Forbidden for requests with unexpected Authorization header.

Observed behavior:
- HTTP 403 responses in runner logs. Flow logs show outbound to S3 and return traffic. TLS handshake completes (proxy performs TLS interception in explicit-proxy mode), but the added Authorization header (and occasionally Proxy-Authorization) causes S3 to reject signed URL validation.

Expected behavior:
- Redwood presigned S3 GETs must succeed when allowed by customer network; egress inspection should not alter headers signed into presigned URL validation.

Logs and diagnostics collected:
- Runner logs (attached): repeated GET <presigned_url> -> 403, with response body: "Access Denied".
- VPC flow logs: TCP accept to s3.amazonaws.com and successful TLS handshake endpoints.
- Packet capture from customer edge (pcap provided): shows proxy injecting Authorization header and rewriting User-Agent.
- Support-run curl test (from customer bastion) reproduces 403 when proxy is in-path, succeeds when traffic bypasses proxy.
- No errors in Redwood control-plane when issuing presigned URLs.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer disabled header-injection rule on proxy for S3 hostnames; downloads returned to normal. This is an acceptable short-term mitigation but customer prefers proxy inspection to remain enabled for other egress.

Suggested long-term mitigations:
1) Customer: Add a proxy rule to avoid injecting Authorization/Proxy-Authorization headers for outbound requests to s3.amazonaws.com and any known presigned hostnames.
2) Customer: Configure explicit CONNECT tunneling for S3 endpoints so that original TLS is preserved (no header mutation).
3) Redwood: Add guidance to Private deployment docs recommending proxy bypass or header-whitelist for presigned URLs and add a preflight check in onboarding that attempts a presigned fetch and warns if intermediate proxies mutate headers.

Attachments:
- pcap_from_customer_edge.pcap
- runner_logs_2026-03-09.txt
- support_curl_test_output.txt
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: corporate proxy is mutating outbound requests (header injection) which breaks presigned URL signature validation. Evidence: pcap shows Authorization header inserted; curl tests bypassing proxy succeed.

Steps taken so far:
- Confirmed presigned URL signature is valid (verified locally by computing canonical request).
- Reproduced failure using customer-provided proxy in a test environment.
- Scoped impact to model artifact downloads only; inference connections and control-plane API calls use different hostnames and are unaffected.
- Created request with minimal headers; proxy still injects Authorization header when request matches '*s3.amazonaws.com*'.

Open questions / next actions:
- Does the proxy inject header for other Redwood endpoints (manifest, policy endpoints)? Customer says only for hosts matched by their egress policy. Need a simple probe run from customer to enumerate.
- Engineering follow-up: consider adding optional metadata on presigned URLs (e.g., a short-lived header token) that proxy rules can detect to route traffic over CONNECT. This is a product-level change and not part of immediate fix.

Owner: Liam Chen (SRE)
Priority: escalate to networking and onboarding docs team to prevent future occurrences.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported widespread 403s for model pulls after rolling out new corporate proxy. They provided pcap and runner logs. Reproduced locally with customer's proxy profile.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen (SRE): Confirmed proxy injects Authorization header which invalidates presigned URL signature. Verified workaround by disabling header-insert rule; downloads succeed. Logging: attached packet captures and curl test logs.

2026-03-11 - Customer (Jared Moreno, Acme Analytics): We need to keep content inspection enabled for compliance. Can Redwood suggest a minimal proxy-rule change? Disabling inspection completely isn't allowed.

2026-03-12 - Liam Chen (SRE): Suggested options to customer: (a) whitelist s3.amazonaws.com for header injection, (b) use CONNECT/CONNECT-HTTPS for S3 endpoints, (c) add lower-level proxy rule to allow specific prefix of presigned URLs. Customer will consult proxy vendor.

2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Triage note: add a KB article to onboarding docs describing 'Proxy header injection and presigned URL failures' and include tests. Filing docs task INT-33210 to track that work.
